text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALARM: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-ded-5' p99 latency > 3s for 7m — streaming sessions experiencing stalls. SLOs: p95<=500ms, p99<=1500ms. Current p95 ~1.2s p99 ~3.4s. Queue depth spiking. Paging on-call (maya).

maya: i'm on it. grabbing recent metrics and queue dumps. any customer visible errors?

charles: support seeing increased errors from customer 'atlas-app' — a lot of aborted streams and reconnects. tickets incoming.

emma: customers: atlas-app (high), a few mid-tier SaaS tests. need to triage impact and decide mitigation (reroute / degrade / throttle).

jason: initial guess: autoscaler didn't provision new hotshot slots fast enough. handshake times spiked and pools were busy. warmup time per instance ~45s due to nvimage pull + kv cache priming.

maya: logs attached show repeated: `handshake timeout waiting for slot` and backlog growth for priority queues.

maya: tail of logs snippet:
```
[12:04:11] pool-manager: allocate_request id=0x4f2 waiting_for_slot
[12:04:12] autoscaler: scale_attempt->pending provisioner=hotshot count=2
[12:04:20] runtime: kv-cache-miss spike seq=0..n
[12:04:50] handshake: slot_ready but stream_init delayed 30s
```

priya: infra note: our new image host in eu-west-2 had intermittent registry throttling for 3rd-party base images earlier today, which would explain image pull slowdowns. i increased parallel pull window but warmup still serialized for kv priming.

jason: also seeing continuous-batching backlog due to large batch size during burst. Batching strategy for dedicated pools kept waiting for batch to fill -> tail amplification. we should temporarily reduce max_batch_size to prefer latency.

maya: concrete mitigation options: 1) emergency scale-up of dedicated pool (if capacity available), 2) reroute non-critical customers to hosted general pool, 3) reduce batching and lower kv priming cost via config toggle, 4) throttle atlas-app to lower concurrency.

emma: prioritize customer-impact mitigation: reroute non-paying/test workloads first, throttle atlas-app only if unavoidable. charles, can support message customers?

charles: yes i'll post ETA: investigating. will message atlas-app that streams may see reconnects and we're working on mitigation.

priya: infra can attempt fast-provision using cached images on spare nodes (image already present on eu-west-2-spare-3). will mark `fast_warmup:true` on new allocations. need runtime change to accept fast_warmup flag.

jason: i can accept the flag. pushing small runtime switch now.

maya: action plan agreed: (A) apply runtime `fast_warmup:true` + reduce `max_batch_size` to 8 for pool eu-west-2-ded-5; (B) reroute non-critical routes -> hosted; (C) monitor p95/p99 and queue depth for 20m; (D) if no improvement, start selective throttle.

jason: rolling change to runtime toggle in 1-2m. patch: `PATCH /runtime/configs/pool/eu-west-2-ded-5 {"fast_warmup": true, "max_batch_size": 8}`

maya: priya — can infra pin images and spin 3 cached nodes now?

priya: starting node spin-up with cached images. command run:
```bash
./provision.sh --region eu-west-2 --count 3 --image cached-eu-west-2:v2 --labels fast_warmup=true
```

priya: spinning, current queue depth dropping from 1200 -> 610 while allocations start.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout patch to runtime-config succeeded on 6/6 hosts in pool.

maya: telemetry update (2m after toggles): p95 -> 640ms, p99 -> 1.6s, queue depth -> 220. improvement but p99 still over SLO.

jason: good sign. still seeing a subset of streams with long first-token delay — likely KV priming for large context models. we can enable aggressive kv-prefix caching for warmup nodes as an intermediate step. i'll prepare a toggle.

emma: charles coordinate customer comms: ping atlas-app that we have partial improvement and expect full recovery in ~15-25m.

charles: posted update to atlas-app: "we're seeing reduced latency, further improvements expected within 20m. engineers are actively provisioning additional capacity."

maya: infra reports 3 cached nodes up and registered. backlog draining rapidly.

priya: note: registry provider confirmed transient throttling window ~11:50-12:10 UTC. they've applied fix. no further pulls should be affected.

maya: 15m check: p95=420ms, p99=980ms, queue depth=60. streaming reconnects dropping.

emma: moving to recovery channel in 25m if stable. please file incident follow-up with root cause: registry throttling + autoscaler handoff slow + batch size sensitivity. include mitigation steps (fast_warmup flag, cached-image pool, reduce max_batch_size for bursts).

jason: i'll open a PR to make `fast_warmup` auto-enable when registry pull latency > X ms and to add a dynamic batch-size policy based on queue depth.

maya: thanks all. closing paging in 10m unless regressions. documented immediate runbook steps in the thread.

ops-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=SEV2, assigned_to=maya, started_at=1755019999, mitigated_at=1755021200

maya: filing short postmortem draft now and adding runbook entries for: pre-warm images, fast_warmup toggle, and fallback routing for dedicated pools.

charles: i'll follow up with customer success on post-incident outreach.

maya: thread summary:
- root cause: intermittent image registry throttling + slow autoscale handoff + batch-size amplifying tail latency
- impact: p99 SLO breach for ~25m, customer-visible reconnects for atlas-app and degraded streaming for some customers
- mitigation: toggle fast_warmup + spin cached nodes + reduce batch_size + reroute non-critical routes
- action items: make warmup auto-detect, improve autoscaler backoff/parallelism, add monitoring alerts for registry pulls

maya: marking incident resolved in pager, will attach PM and timeline to the follow-up. :white_check_mark:
